summary: http2 GOAWAY propagation plus ephemeral-disk throttle causing GPU watchdog resets and 5xx wave
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 08:50 UTC we observed an elevated 5xx error rate from the us-east API gateway localized to a small set of dedicated customer routes (BrightForms). The 5xxs coincide with a pattern of API Gateway HTTP/2 GOAWAY frames being propagated to upstream proxies, followed by increased disk I/O wait on ephemeral NVMe volumes attached to runtime pods, then GPU driver watchdog resets causing runtimes to exit. Impact: ~40% of requests for the customer routes returning 5xx (502/503) for ~25 minutes. Customer reports degraded streaming performance and failed batch embeddings. This ticket captures SRE + Support investigation, mitigations applied, and next steps for a post-incident action item.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Route synthetic traffic that opens long-lived HTTP/2 streams and high connection churn against the affected customer route (simulate BrightForms traffic patterns).
2) Inject a transient storage throttle on ephemeral NVMe (stress i/o for ~30s) on a subset of runtime nodes.
3) Observe GOAWAY propagation from API gateway to upstream proxies, increased request queues, and eventual runtime GPU watchdog resets in logs.
logs: [2026-03-10T08:51:12Z] apigw[proxy-01] INFO received GOAWAY for conn_id=0x7f4f: last_stream=1234; reason=load_shed
[2026-03-10T08:51:18Z] node-runtime-08 kernel: blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 123456
[2026-03-10T08:51:25Z] runtime[redwood-runtime] ERROR gpu_watchdog: saw Xid 13; initiating watchdog reset
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: API gateway began returning GOAWAY to upstreams due to transient accept-queue pressure; that pushed load to fewer runtime pods which magnified ephemeral disk I/O and triggered driver stalls.
SRE checked node-level metrics (iostat, dstat) and saw NVMe latency spikes (avg>50ms) on three runtime nodes at the incident start time.
Servicing model prefetch and KV cache write-backs were concentrated due to autoscaler not adding nodes fast enough (scale-up lag ~45s under the burst).
GPU watchdog Xid 13 indicates a GPU hang likely tied to heavy CUDA pagefaults during KV prefetch hitting high disk latency (correlated in node dmesg).
We found an autoscaler threshold misconfiguration: scale-up policy uses cpu_utilization target only and ignores ephemeral-disk-iowait which allowed oversubscription.
A customer-side spike pattern amplified the issue: BrightForms had a timed batch upload which opened many long-lived streams causing HTTP/2 session churn and more connections per runtime.
mitigations_applied: 1) Temporarily disabled long-lived-streams on the affected route via route-level short-stream policy to reduce connection churn.
2) Bounced 3 impacted runtime pods to clear GPU watchdog state and allow KV caches to warm on healthy nodes.
3) Raised autoscaler aggressiveness for ephemeral-disk-iowait signals (hotfix) to allow faster node add during IO pressure.
4) Added an immediate apigw-side backoff (50ms) for new HTTP/2 accept attempts to smooth storm of new connections.
resolution: Partial mitigation achieved: error rate dropped from ~40% to ~2% within 6 minutes after mitigations. No data loss observed; most requests retried successfully. Root-cause chain: HTTP/2 GOAWAY propagation and connection churn reduced effective pooled capacity -> concentrated prefetch + KV write-back I/O on a small set of ephemeral NVMe devices -> elevated disk latency caused CUDA page faults and GPU watchdog resets. Full fix requires autoscaler logic change and better IO isolation for runtimes.
next_steps: 1) Engineering to implement autoscaler telemetry on disk_iowait and include it in scale-up policy (owner: infra-autoscaler).
2) Platform to add IO QoS guardrails for runtime pods (limit prefetch writeback concurrency) (owner: serving-runtime).
3) Support to contact BrightForms with recommended SDK pattern change for long-lived-stream batching to reduce connection churn (owner: CSM).
4) Postmortem and runbook update linking GOAWAY detection -> autoscale IO mitigation path (owner: SRE).
5) Add a synthetic test that replicates long-lived-stream + batch-upload mix to detect regressions in pre-prod.
